current_activity: command post moves 120 miles to Lesneven to open the siege of Brest
notes: Event date: Breakout-30 p638: on 18 August the VIII Corps command post moved one hundred and twenty miles to Lesneven, fifteen miles from Brest, to undertake the siege. Event definition: headquarters move. Location: Lesneven town centroid. Later: no source used places the corps headquarters anywhere else before 24 September (St Aubin, CMH list), so Lesneven is the only documented headquarters for the 5 and 10 September command rows; those rows keep their Brest-sector points because the headquarters is not documented on those dates. Relationship: Third Army assigned. Coordinate check: the speed warning against C0313 (17 August) is the documented 120-mile move; the earlier point is the corps position before the move. Batch 2 review: Lesneven is a documented headquarters observation for 18 August. It is the last confirmed headquarters location before the CMH list's St Aubin on 24 September, not a verified position for each day between; the 5 and 10 September rows (C0315, C0316) do not use it as such. The speed warning against C0313 is an explained exception (data/coordinate_exceptions.csv).

current_activity: opening the main attack on Brest with 29th, 8th and 2nd Divisions
notes: Breakout-30 p641: Middleton set the main attack for the afternoon of 25 August with 29th Division on the right, 8th in the center and 2nd on the left. Objective check (Batch 2 review): the corps attack opened at the town on the row date, so documented_on_date holds.

current_activity: receiving the capitulation of German forces in eastern Brest and Recouvrance
notes: Event date: Breakout-30 p650: both German capitulations at Brest occurred on 18 September (Recouvrance to the 29th Division, the east of the city to the 2nd Division); the garrison commanders were von der Mosel (29th Division sector) and Pietzonka (2nd Division sector). Event definition: surrender of the German forces holding Brest and Recouvrance. Ramcke, the fortress commander, had escaped to the Crozon peninsula and surrendered there on 19 September (see the alternate row), so the garrison did not surrender in a single act. Relationship: Ninth Army (VIII Corps passed to it on 10 September).

Event date: Wikipedia gives 19 September for the liberation of Brest. Event definition: 19 September is the day Ramcke surrendered on the Crozon peninsula, ending organised resistance in the Brest area (Breakout-30 p650); it is not a separate capture of the city, which capitulated on 18 September (preferred row). The point stays at Brest; Crozon is about 20 km to the south-west.

current_activity: corps headquarters and 2nd, 8th Divisions leaving Brest for Belgium and Luxembourg
notes: Breakout-30 p653: on 26 September VIII Corps headquarters and the 2nd and 8th Divisions began moving by rail and motor to Belgium and Luxembourg, still under Ninth Army; the 29th Division left for First Army on 24 September.

current_activity: most of the headquarters leaves Bastogne for Neufchâteau; Middleton stays in Bastogne with a small staff
notes: Event date: 18 December 1944 (Ardennes p287: telephone service to the VIII Corps headquarters at Bastogne ended on 18 December when that headquarters moved to Neufchâteau; p314, in the account of 18 December: "As ordered by General Hodges, most of the VIII Corps headquarters moved during the day to Neufchâteau"). Event definition: the corps command post splits: the main staff goes to Neufchâteau, about eighteen miles south-west of Bastogne, and the corps commander remains in Bastogne to brief the arriving airborne and armored commanders (p314). Neufchâteau is therefore the headquarters point; Bastogne remains in use for a few more days. Relationship: First Army assigned from 22 October (Siegfried p378). Location: Neufchâteau commune centroid; the atlas lists the command post at Neufchâteau from 20 December (two days later). Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim: Neufchâteau, Luxembourg, Wallonie, 6840, België / Belgique / Belgien. Event support: high (two Green Book pages agree on the date and the order from Hodges). Location support: moderate (the place is documented for the date, but only for most of the staff; the commander stayed in Bastogne).

current_activity: passes from First Army to Third Army
notes: Event date: 20 December 1944 (Ardennes p399: "The VIII Corps passed to General Patton's Third Army during the 20th", word of which was brought to the 101st trains by Colonel Ryan from the VIII Corps headquarters in Neufchâteau). The hour is not documented. Event definition: the corps and the units attached to it, including the 101st Airborne at Bastogne, pass from Hodges' First Army to Patton's Third Army; the same day Eisenhower's order puts First and Ninth Armies under 21st Army Group. Relationship (sequence): First Army assigned until the passage; Third Army assigned from the passage; both are listed on 20 December, the boundary day, because the hour is not documented (effective_to is inclusive, so the First Army entry ends on 20 December; its earliest possible end is 19 December). The row's parent is Third Army, the headquarters the event passes the corps to; the corps' controller at a given hour of 20 December is unknown. Location: Atlas and Green Book agree on Neufchâteau on 20 December (p399, p321: the corps re-forming around Neufchâteau and Arlon on 21 December). Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim: Neufchâteau, Luxembourg, Wallonie, 6840, België / Belgique / Belgien. Event support: high (Green Book narrative; hour not documented). Location support: high for the place (atlas and narrative on the date).
